title: How do you start a conversation and keep it going?
examples: How do I start talking to someone new?
What do I say when a conversation goes quiet?

steps.label: Ask a follow-up
steps.ask: How do I keep a conversation going?

explain.say: Imagine standing next to someone at the bus stop, both of you silent, and you want to say something but your mind goes blank. Here is a secret recipe! Look at the first step on the board: notice something, like their book or T-shirt.

draw.text: How do you start a conversation and keep it going?

steps.label: Ask a follow-up
steps.ask: How do I keep a conversation going?

explain.say: Then smile and say hi: Hi, I am Noor. Now see the speech bubble? Ask an open question, like, what is that book about? Can you think of an open question to ask someone?

steps.label: Ask a follow-up
steps.ask: How do I keep a conversation going?

explain.say: Next, listen and look interested. Then ask a follow-up, a question about what they just said: which part was the best? And share about you: I love adventure books too! See the steps ticking off?

steps.label: Ask a follow-up
steps.ask: How do I keep a conversation going?

explain.say: Now the secret. A closed question, like, do you like football, gets a yes or no, and the chat can stop fast. Look at the left side of the board. Can you hear how short it is?

draw.name: x-compare
draw.verdict: Open questions open up a conversation

explain.say: An open question, like, what do you like about football, gets a whole story, and the chat keeps going. Super! Wow fact: a Harvard study found people who ask more follow-up questions are liked more.

draw.name: x-compare
draw.verdict: Open questions open up a conversation

faq.a: A question that needs more than yes or no, often starting with what, how or why, like: What do you like about drawing?
asks: Tell me about the Open question

faq.q: How do I keep a conversation going?
faq.a: Ask follow-up questions about what they said, share a little about yourself, and listen. If it goes quiet, ask about something you both see or like.
asks: What do I say when a conversation goes quiet?
Tell me about the Ask a follow-up

faq.a: A question that can be answered with yes or no, like: Do you like pizza? It is fine to start with, but follow it with an open question.
asks: Tell me about the Closed question

faq.q: What can I talk about with someone new?
faq.a: Things around you, school, games, books, shows, pets, food or weekend plans. Noticing something they have is an easy start.
asks: Tell me about the Notice something

faq.q: What if I feel nervous starting a conversation?
faq.a: Lots of people do. Plan one question ahead, take a breath, and start small. It gets easier every time you practise.
asks: I get nervous talking to people

facts: A 2017 Harvard study by Karen Huang and colleagues found that people who asked more questions, especially follow-up questions, were liked more by their conversation partners.
Open questions often begin with what, how or why, while closed questions can be answered with yes or no.

quiz.why: It needs more than yes or no, so the chat keeps going.

wrong.0: This can be answered yes or no.
wrong.2: This can be answered yes or no.

quiz.say: Your new friend says: I went to the beach. What is a good follow-up?
quiz.why: A follow-up asks more about what they said.
